minutes.headline: Committee approved paying the bus contractors half of unused contract amounts, lifted the hiring freeze, and passed the SOA plan.
minutes.summary: Final meeting for the two outgoing members, with farewells and plaques. The committee approved the Student Opportunity Act plan, the extended day handbook, the superintendent evaluation, removal of the hiring freeze, a payment to the bus vendors for unrendered service, and a lunch donation application. Extended day rate increases, ESSER grant use, and the handbook template were discussed without votes.

public_comment.topic: Resident urged the committee to engage on the revenue side and advocate for school funding, warning that state aid cuts could be larger than expected.

what_happened.line: The School Committee voted 4-0, with one member recused, to pay bus vendors up to a recommended amount for service not rendered during the pandemic closure.
The committee voted 5-0 to remove the hiring freeze, so positions budgeted for the new fiscal year can be filled.
The committee voted 5-0 to approve the Student Opportunity Act plan for fiscal years 21 through 23.
The committee also voted 5-0 on the extended day handbook changes, the superintendent evaluation, the personnel report and a lunch donation.
Administration plans to use ESSER grant funds for staffing and stipends, which the committee agreed to without a vote. The next meeting was set for June 30.

why_it_matters: The bus payment and the plan to use the unspent transportation money to prepay out-of-district tuition both come from this year's school budget, which is funded mostly by taxes.
Lifting the hiring freeze lets budgeted positions be filled, and the Student Opportunity Act plan adds one new special education teacher beyond the approved budget.
Extended day and early learning rates may rise, and the finance committee has only a set-aside for a state aid cut, so a larger cut would need more money.
